findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: AC5's merge base — 'the prior persisted full snapshot' — does not exist in the codebase as a full snapshot; the persisted prev artifact stores only key membership with empty bodies, so upserting a delta onto it produces a snapshot whose unchanged entries have empty field bodies.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC5 ('merged onto the prior persisted full snapshot ... upsert')
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step to persist the full per-pass snapshot as the durable merge base (or reuse `bridge_state/snapshots/<pass_id>.json` deliberately), and state that the incremental upsert overlays that full-content base — not the current key-only `prev_snapshot.json`.

findings.finding: AC5 places the merge at `_build_snapshot` in fetcher.py, but the prior snapshot needed as the merge base is loaded in reconcile.py `_load_snapshots`, and `_build_snapshot(pass_id, repo_root)` has no parameter or access path to prior state — the chosen insertion point cannot see the data it must merge onto.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC5 ('the incremental result enters at snapshot assembly in fetcher.py _build_snapshot')
findings.suggested_fix: Perform the upsert in reconcile.py after `curr_snapshot` is fetched incrementally and `prev_snapshot` (full form) is loaded, producing the merged snapshot before the differ runs; keep `_build_snapshot` responsible only for the incremental fetch.

findings.finding: AC5 specifies no behaviour when the merge base is empty, absent, or corrupt; on a fresh run prev_snapshot is `{}`, so an incremental delta merged onto `{}` yields an incomplete snapshot presented as complete — the exact mass-deletion read AC5 exists to prevent.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC5 (merge mechanism) and AC2 (full-scan fallback)
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'incremental is used only when a complete, non-corrupt prior snapshot exists; otherwise the pass performs a full scan' — mirroring the existing corrupt-prev abort in `_handle_corrupt_snapshot`.

The watermark returned by search_incremental (AC4, 'the watermark to resume from') has no specified lifecycle: who persists it, when it is written, what a consumer does on the FIRST run when no watermark exists, and whether a lost/absent watermark safely degrades to a full scan.
findings.location: AC4 ('returns the watermark to resume from')
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'The resume watermark is persisted per (backend, scope) after a merged snapshot is written; when no watermark exists (first run, cleared state) the caller performs a full scan and seeds the watermark from it.'

findings.finding: AC4 says the capability 'returns the watermark to resume from', which is stateful across reconciliation passes, but the plan does not specify the watermark's lifecycle: who persists it, where it is stored, how it is read back on the next pass, and how it is initialized/retired. The resume point is shared state whose CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME/RETIRE path is undefined.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC4 and 'return type must carry the next watermark' (§2)
